tasks.short: Prepare HR reports showing hiring, onboarding, retention, absence and workforce costs for managers.

today.trigger: A reporting deadline or a manager's request. This workflow is inferred from the supplied systems; current handling times need measurement.
steps: Pull the latest AFAS-based Power BI figures and relevant Recruitee or Studytube exports.
Check reporting dates, headcount definitions, cohort maturity and missing records.
Build the requested site, department or employment-type breakdown in Power BI or Excel.
Explain changes, check sensitive breakdowns and distribute the report.
drudgery: Repeating the same filters and reconciliations
today.time_sinks: Resolving inconsistent denominators, checking incomplete 90-day cohorts and assembling custom breakdowns.

lenses.faster: Scheduled extracts, reconciliations and report templates remove repeated assembly. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 18 minutes for exception checks, interpretation and review; unfamiliar custom requests take longer.
lenses.autonomous: A successful nightly refresh starts validation and report production; approved reports are distributed automatically when checks pass. New definitions, sensitive cuts and unexplained movements require analyst approval.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give the three site management teams a weekly vacancy-to-day-90 review that connects hiring, onboarding and retention. Demand would likely grow as the preparation cost falls.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying figures between Excel and slides. More time goes into explaining why a site loses new starters and testing practical improvements with managers.
lenses.options: Show hiring more people, improving offer acceptance and improving first-week onboarding as separate scenarios. Different assumptions can change which intervention the HR Director funds.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward investigating exceptions and evaluating interventions. With delegated authority to accept report definitions and block unreliable releases, the role becomes more expert in measurement and interpretation.
reach: Absorb the HR Business Partner's recurring site workforce pack preparation; learn operational staffing decisions and each site's CAO context.
Absorb the FP&A Analyst's preparation of workforce-volume inputs; learn cost-centre mapping and payroll-to-ledger reconciliation.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst must distinguish a real operational change from a definition change and challenge unsupported explanations, especially when retention or absence figures could influence decisions about people.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: approved calculations, checks, templates and delivery schedules can be written down. Free-form generated commentary is unnecessary for the core reporting workflow.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract and required supplementary feeds complete successfully.
steps: Validate freshness, record counts and reconciliation totals; stop affected reports when checks fail.
Calculate approved measures with documented employee and flex-worker populations and mature 90-day cohorts.
Generate approved reports with source dates, definitions and access restrictions.
Send passing standard reports to authorised recipients and queue exceptions or new custom cuts for review.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves first publication, metric changes, new recipient groups and sensitive custom breakdowns; established reports run without approval each time.
systems: Power BI semantic model and subscriptions
Approved Recruitee and Studytube exports or feeds
data_needed: Employment dates, site, department, contracted hours and employment type
Vacancy, offer and hire dates
Onboarding completion and an agreed manager-confirmed definition of productive
Absence rates and durations under restricted access, without medical causes
Approved reporting populations, suppression rules and recipient permissions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint reporting register records source timestamps, definition versions, checks, exceptions and report releases.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports report summaries and questions over a prepared semantic model; Microsoft warns that poor preparation can cause misinterpretation.
Scheduled calculations and report templates can remove repeated assembly; the 70% saving is an unmeasured planning estimate for this task mix.
Absence reporting requires special care because health data receives additional GDPR protection.

risks: A technically correct report can still use the wrong cohort or denominator.
Nightly extracts can be mistaken for live staffing information.
Small groups can reveal sensitive information even when names are removed.
The productive-hire measure could become employee performance monitoring and require OR involvement.
research_questions: What share of requests uses stable templates, and how much time remains after automated assembly?
Can AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube records be linked reliably using an authorised identifier?
How will managers confirm productivity consistently across warehouse, transport and office jobs?
Which proposed measures and reporting facilities require OR consent before introduction?

tasks.short: Get reliable HR figures to the right managers on time.

today.trigger: A report becomes due, a refresh fails or a manager asks for the latest figures; the detailed workflow is inferred.
steps: Check whether the Power BI refresh and source exports have completed.
Identify the appropriate report, audience and access permissions.
Send links or files and explain reporting dates or known limitations.
Chase failed deliveries, access problems and missing inputs.
drudgery: Answering requests for the same report link
today.time_sinks: Following up on missing inputs and resolving confusion about which version is current.

lenses.faster: Refresh checks, subscriptions and approved routing replace manual chasing and repeat messages. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 18 minutes of exception handling and service review.
lenses.autonomous: A completed refresh or missed deadline starts checks, publication and approved notifications. Failures, unusual recipient changes and access requests go to the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Group served for the first time: night-shift supervisors receive an approved staffing and onboarding brief before their shift through an accessible channel. Demand would likely grow if delivery becomes dependable and cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing refreshes or resending attachments. The analyst gets more time to understand whether managers can act on the information.
lenses.options: Compare daily alerts, weekly digests and shift-start delivery by audience. This changes whether managers receive useful information in time or simply get more messages.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from distributing reports to managing an HR information service. Proposed decision rights include setting delivery standards, withholding stale information and agreeing escalation routes with data owners.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's routine reminders for missing reporting inputs; learn ownership of AFAS fields and escalation responsibilities.
Absorb the HR Business Partner's forwarding of recurring workforce packs; learn which decisions each management audience makes.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges when a late or incomplete report would mislead managers and negotiates useful delivery expectations across shifts and sites.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: freshness checks, recipient lists, schedules and escalation rules are predictable. A model is unnecessary for routine delivery.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled delivery window arrives or a refresh reports success or failure.
steps: Check source freshness and the validation result for each scheduled report.
Publish the current approved version and deliver access-controlled links to approved audiences.
Suppress stale delivery and notify the responsible data owner when a check fails.
Queue unresolved failures and requested audience changes for the analyst.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves audiences, access changes and delivery policies; routine delivery follows the approved configuration.
systems: Power BI refresh monitoring and subscriptions
Scheduled monitoring workflow, subject to connector and licence checks
data_needed: Refresh and validation status
Report owners and delivery deadlines
Approved recipient groups and access permissions
Shift schedules and available communication channels
Escalation contacts
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint service log records freshness, delivery status, failures and approved routing changes.

evidence.claim: Scheduled report delivery and refresh monitoring can operate through deterministic workflow rules; the 70% saving needs local validation.
Microsoft reports that faster access to HR information does not by itself establish better decisions.

risks: An automated distribution list can expose information after a manager changes roles.
Successful delivery does not prove the report was useful or understood.
Night-shift supervisors may lack suitable accounts or time to access the brief.
research_questions: Which delivery failures and repeat requests consume the most analyst time?
Do all intended shift supervisors have authorised access to the proposed channel?
Can current Power BI licences and refresh monitoring support the required delivery schedule?
Which information must be ready before a shift starts, and can a nightly extract meet that need?

tasks.short: Keep AFAS reporting feeds, Power BI dashboards and HR measures working correctly.

today.trigger: A refresh fails, a source field changes or HR requests a dashboard update; the maintenance process is inferred.
steps: Inspect the affected feed, query, measure or visual.
Trace the issue to source data, transformation logic, permissions or a changed definition.
Update SQL, Power Query, DAX or dashboard configuration.
Reconcile representative results and check access before publishing.
Document the change and notify affected users.
systems: SQL or scripts where actually deployed
drudgery: Tracing field names through several transformations
Writing repetitive DAX or query changes
today.time_sinks: Understanding dependencies and proving that a small change has not altered retention, absence or workforce totals.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts query changes, explains dependencies and prepares reconciliation checks and documentation. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 36 minutes, including analyst diagnosis, testing and release review.
lenses.autonomous: A failed refresh or change request opens a maintenance item with diagnostics and suggested fixes. The analyst decides the cause, edits the solution and approves publication.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give Payroll and Finance a shared explanation of headcount, paid hours and workforce-cost differences at month close. Demand would likely grow when reconciliation becomes easier.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting for renamed columns or writing boilerplate documentation. More time goes into making measures trustworthy and simplifying fragile reporting dependencies.
lenses.options: Compare repairing a local measure, changing the shared model or changing the source capture. The alternatives can change maintenance cost and consistency across every downstream report.
lenses.altitude: The week includes more model design and fewer repetitive edits. Proposed authority to approve semantic-model changes and reject unsupported measures makes the role more technically expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller's initial investigation of workforce-reporting discrepancies; learn payroll-to-ledger mappings and financial materiality.
Absorb the Payroll Specialist's preparation of reporting reconciliation evidence; learn pay periods, retroactive corrections and CAO-related pay components.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst understands which change preserves business meaning, notices misleading but plausible calculations and accepts responsibility for release quality.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: changes require technical diagnosis and business judgment. Generated SQL or DAX is useful drafting support but cannot safely establish correctness.

in_practice.trigger: A refresh alert or approved dashboard change enters the maintenance queue.
steps: Collect error details, model metadata and a sanitised example of the discrepancy.
Ask the copilot for possible causes, draft changes and relevant reconciliation checks.
Have the analyst select and implement the change in a controlled test version.
Compare source totals, historical cohorts and role-based views before publication.
Publish the approved version and record the reason and rollback reference.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst controls diagnosis, implementation and production release; Payroll or the Controller approves changes to definitions they own.
systems: Power BI development and production environments
data_needed: Schemas and measure definitions
Refresh errors and dependency information
Sanitised examples and reconciliation totals
Access rules and source-owner approvals
Prior model version
in_practice.logs_to: The restricted change register stores the issue, reviewed change, validation results, approver and released version.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can write DAX and assist report creation, subject to capacity and model-preparation requirements.
Uber documented faster query authoring with QueryGPT while identifying hallucinated tables and columns as an unresolved problem; its result does not establish Noordhaven's saving.
The 40% end-to-end saving is a planning estimate that retains diagnosis, testing and release review.

risks: Generated code can run successfully while calculating the wrong business measure.
A shared-model change can silently alter multiple dashboards.
Personal data or credentials could be exposed through diagnostic prompts.
Power BI Copilot capacity requirements may make the proposed tool unavailable.
research_questions: Which maintenance categories account for most hours, and how much involves repetitive code?
Is suitable Power BI capacity available, and is the proposed assistant approved for this data?
Are there reliable reference totals and a controlled place to test changes?
Who can approve changes to payroll, retention and absence definitions?

tasks.short: Help HR colleagues and managers resolve problems with reports and dashboards.

today.trigger: A colleague reports an incorrect figure, access problem or difficulty using a dashboard.
steps: Ask for the report, filters, expected result and relevant error details.
Reproduce the problem using the appropriate permissions.
Check freshness, definitions, source records and access configuration.
Explain the answer or route a confirmed defect to maintenance.
Record reusable guidance and confirm resolution.
drudgery: Explaining the same filters and definitions
today.time_sinks: Reproducing problems caused by filters, permissions or different expectations of the same metric.

lenses.faster: A copilot structures the request, suggests checks and drafts an answer from approved guidance. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 36 minutes for reproduction, judgment and reviewed communication.
lenses.autonomous: A support request starts a fixed intake and retrieval step that assembles relevant guidance. The analyst checks the diagnosis and sends the response or performs the fix.
lenses.ambitious: Group served for the first time: supervisors on evening and night shifts get a structured support intake and an approved guide they can use outside office hours. Demand would likely grow as access improves.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss repeatedly asking which filters were selected. More time goes into teaching managers how to interpret information and fixing recurring causes.
lenses.options: Compare a clearer definition, a redesigned visual and a short training intervention for recurring requests. These alternatives change whether the underlying confusion disappears.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward improving report usability and reducing recurring incidents. Proposed authority to prioritise usability fixes adds product judgment while retaining technical expertise.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's first-line answers about dashboard navigation; learn common supervisor workflows and permission boundaries.
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's preparation of short dashboard guides; learn accessible instruction for shift workers.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst recognises when an apparently simple question signals a faulty definition, an access issue or a manager about to make an unsupported people decision.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the analyst remains responsible for troubleshooting and communication. A guided intake and retrieved draft are sufficient without an open-ended agent.

in_practice.trigger: A manager or HR colleague submits a report-support request.
steps: Capture the report link, issue, filters and source timestamp without collecting unnecessary employee details.
Retrieve approved definitions and known fixes relevant to the request.
Prepare a suggested diagnosis, checks and draft response for the analyst.
Have the analyst reproduce the problem, resolve it or create a maintenance item.
Record the verified answer in the support knowledge base.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst verifies each diagnosis and response; access changes follow the existing data-owner approval process.
data_needed: Report and page identifiers
Selected filters and error text
Current metric definitions and known fixes
Requester role and authorised scope
Refresh and incident status
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted support register records the request, sources consulted, verified resolution and any maintenance follow-up.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot can answer questions over a prepared model; Microsoft warns about misinterpretation and does not officially support non-English chat.
Approved-guidance retrieval and response drafting can assist technical support; the 40% saving is an unmeasured planning estimate.

risks: A convincing explanation can conceal an unresolved source-data defect.
Support screenshots may contain employee or absence information.
Dutch terminology and CAO concepts may be mistranslated.
Guidance written for one permission level may fail for another.
research_questions: What proportion of support requests repeats a documented question?
Can the analyst reproduce each audience's permissions without broadening access?
Does the assistant handle Noordhaven's Dutch metric names and CAO vocabulary reliably?
Does drafting reduce total resolution time once verification and corrections are included?

tasks.short: Find managers and HR teams whose workforce information needs are not being met.

today.trigger: A service review or repeated request suggests an unmet need. Here, 'customers' is interpreted as internal HR-information users; commercial customer analysis is outside this role.
steps: Review approved report-use summaries, support requests and stakeholder feedback.
Group needs by site, role and workforce decision.
Identify audiences with repeated requests or poor access to existing information.
Discuss the apparent gap with the relevant manager or HR Business Partner.
Prioritise a reporting, access or training response.
drudgery: Checking which teams receive each report
today.time_sinks: Separating a real information gap from low report usage caused by access, timing or an irrelevant dashboard.

lenses.faster: Approved request categories and service-coverage checks replace manual counting and matching. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 27 minutes for validating gaps and discussing priorities with users.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly service review runs agreed checks on aggregate demand, delivery coverage and unresolved requests. The analyst validates apparent gaps before contacting teams or changing priorities.
lenses.ambitious: New service: offer the Venlo site management team a workforce-information needs review that leads to a specific reporting or training intervention. Demand could grow if the review becomes inexpensive and demonstrably useful.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss counting repeated requests in mail threads. More time goes into understanding the decisions that underserved managers struggle to make.
lenses.options: Compare extending an existing dashboard, changing delivery timing and providing training. The choice changes both the service offered and which audience benefits.
lenses.altitude: The week includes deliberate service discovery across sites. Proposed authority to prioritise the HR analytics backlog makes the role more expert in internal customer needs as well as data.
reach: Absorb the HR Business Partner's collection of recurring workforce-information requests; learn site planning cycles and manager interviews.
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's initial identification of dashboard-training demand; learn needs assessment without treating low usage as poor performance.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst establishes trust, discovers needs people have not expressed and avoids treating tool usage as a measure of individual engagement or competence.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: structured service requests, approved audience lists and coverage rules can generate a checkable gap list. Interviews and prioritisation remain with the analyst.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly HR analytics service review becomes due.
steps: Read structured request categories, unresolved items and approved audience-level service measures.
Compare service coverage with agreed needs by site, shift and management role.
Produce an internal gap list with supporting counts and known limitations.
Have the analyst validate priorities with affected users before commissioning changes.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine gap detection runs automatically; the analyst approves interpretations, stakeholder outreach and backlog changes. Any new monitoring capability receives the required privacy and OR assessment first.
systems: Power BI approved aggregate service measures
data_needed: Structured request categories and resolution status
Approved report audiences and delivery coverage
Site and role-level feedback
Agreed service expectations
Any authorised aggregate usage measures
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted service-review register records inputs, detected gaps, validation outcomes and agreed priorities.

evidence.claim: This task's internal-customer interpretation is an assumption requiring validation against Noordhaven's actual role scope.
evidence.source: Role-scoping assumption based on the supplied HR team context

evidence.claim: Structured demand and coverage rules can automate preparation of a service-gap list; the 55% saving is a planning estimate.
Dutch works-council consent rights cover arrangements involving personal data and facilities capable of monitoring employee presence, behaviour or performance.

risks: The O*NET task may not correspond to work this analyst actually performs.
Low usage can reflect poor access or irrelevant content rather than low demand.
Usage monitoring can introduce employee-monitoring capabilities even if outputs are aggregated.
Office users may dominate recorded demand while shift supervisors remain unheard.
research_questions: Does this task actually mean internal service discovery in Noordhaven's analyst role?
Are enough requests captured consistently to support rules-based gap detection?
Can gaps be identified from requests and delivery coverage without adding individual usage tracking?
Would supervisors at all three sites act on a service-needs review?

tasks.short: Build HR dashboards and data models that answer agreed workforce questions.

today.trigger: HR or a site manager requests a new decision tool, dashboard or reporting dataset.
steps: Clarify the decision, audience, definitions and source ownership.
Inspect available AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube or agency data and design the joins.
Build transformations, measures and a usable report or spreadsheet.
Reconcile outputs and test access and sensitive-group handling.
Review with users, publish and document maintenance responsibilities.
today.time_sinks: Agreeing definitions, establishing trustworthy joins and testing whether the tool supports the intended decision.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts schemas, transformations, DAX and prototype layouts from an agreed specification. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 36 minutes because requirements, reconciliation and user acceptance still take substantial work.
lenses.autonomous: An approved brief starts drafting of the model, measures and documentation. The analyst selects the design, implements it and obtains acceptance before production use.
lenses.ambitious: Group served for the first time: give staffing-agency coordinators an authorised aggregate onboarding and certificate-readiness view for flex workers at the three sites. Demand would likely grow in peak season if it replaces manual checks.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss recreating the same date tables or documentation. More time goes into solving the user's problem and designing clear measures.
lenses.options: Prototype separate views for site managers, HR Business Partners and agency coordinators. Comparing them can reveal that different decisions require different data, access and refresh frequency.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward designing shared HR data products. Proposed authority to accept data contracts and require access controls makes the role more expert in architecture, privacy and user needs.
reach: Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's certificate-status dashboard construction; learn certificate validity and authorised evidence requirements.
Absorb the FP&A Analyst's workforce-scenario tool construction; learn financial modelling assumptions and cost reconciliation.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst decides what should be built, whether the data can support it and whether a convincing prototype would create misleading or intrusive decision-making.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: code and prototypes are draftable, but requirements, architecture, access and acceptance require sustained analyst leadership. The supplied automation classification does not establish safe autonomous deployment.

in_practice.trigger: A data owner approves a brief specifying the decision, users and permitted data.
steps: Specify measures, source contracts, refresh needs and access boundaries.
Use an approved copilot to draft transformations, measures and a prototype using synthetic or minimised data.
Have the analyst implement and reconcile the selected design.
Test representative user permissions, small-group handling and source failures.
Obtain user and data-owner acceptance, publish and assign ongoing ownership.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the design and release; relevant data owners approve sharing, and OR consent is obtained where required before introducing the facility.
data_needed: Approved source schemas and join keys
Metric definitions and acceptance examples
User roles and permitted sharing scope
Flex-worker agency affiliations and authorised onboarding records
Certificate dates and statuses where necessary and lawfully available
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted product register stores the brief, model versions, validation evidence, access approvals and release acceptance.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot assists with report creation and DAX over a prepared model.
Uber's documented text-to-SQL experience supports faster drafting but also demonstrates the need to verify generated queries.
The proposed flex-worker service and 40% saving are design hypotheses, not documented outcomes at Noordhaven.

risks: Agency data may lack consistent identifiers or reliable refresh arrangements.
A prototype can look finished before definitions and access rules are settled.
External sharing can reveal another agency's workers or commercially sensitive information.
Adding performance evaluation or behaviour-based task allocation could change the EU AI Act classification.
research_questions: Which build steps dominate current effort, and how much can drafting actually remove?
Can the three agencies supply consistent data under suitable sharing arrangements?
Who owns and approves certificate validity and onboarding-readiness definitions?
Does the proposed use require OR consent or employment-related AI obligations, and what rules apply at deployment?

tasks.short: Check HR records and compile reliable figures on hires, transfers and absence.

today.trigger: The nightly extract, a reporting deadline or a discrepancy raises the need to check personnel records.
steps: Extract authorised employment events and absence fields from AFAS.
Check missing dates, inconsistent statuses, duplicate records and reporting populations.
Ask HR Administration or Payroll to verify and correct source records.
Compile and reconcile personnel statistics by approved group.
Record limitations and release the statistics to authorised users.
drudgery: Matching corrected records back to reports
today.time_sinks: Resolving ambiguous records with source owners and distinguishing genuine open absence records from missing closure updates.

lenses.faster: Rules check record completeness, produce correction queues and recalculate approved statistics after correction. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 15 minutes for exception review and source-owner follow-up; no time is saved by silently shifting unresolved work to HR Administration.
lenses.autonomous: Each successful nightly extract starts validation and compilation. Routine passing statistics publish automatically; source corrections and uncertain records go to the responsible human.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: HR Business Partners can review reconciled site-level absence and starter-cohort movements each working day instead of waiting for a reporting pack. Demand would likely grow if fresh checks require little preparation.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss finding the same missing end dates repeatedly. More time goes into preventing source-data problems and explaining meaningful workforce changes.
lenses.options: Compare a source-field validation, a clearer administrative procedure and a reconciliation rule for each recurring defect. The choice changes whether the error is prevented or merely detected later.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from correcting reporting symptoms to improving HR data quality. Proposed authority to define release thresholds and escalate recurring defects makes the role more expert without transferring employment-record decisions from HR Administration.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's routine completeness checking and correction-list preparation; learn AFAS event workflows and record ownership.
Absorb the Payroll Specialist's preparation of standard personnel-count reconciliations; learn payroll cut-offs and retroactive employment changes.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst recognises ambiguous employment histories and inappropriate inferences from absence data; authorised HR staff establish the facts and correct personnel records.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: completeness checks, event counts and reconciliations follow explicit rules. Neither record correction nor medical interpretation should be delegated to a model.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract passes freshness checks.
steps: Validate required dates, event sequences, identifiers and approved status combinations.
Create a restricted exception queue with the rule failed and source-record reference.
Route corrections to HR Administration or Payroll and track resolution without automatic source edits.
Recalculate authorised statistics and reconcile changes against the previous extract.
Release passing outputs and hold affected figures when unresolved exceptions exceed approved tolerances.
in_practice.human_gate: Authorised HR staff approve source-record corrections; the analyst reviews ambiguous exceptions and approves changes to validation or release rules.
data_needed: Employment start and end dates, transfers and authorised statuses
Site, department, contracted hours and reporting population
Restricted absence dates, duration and administrative status without medical causes
Approved appraisal completion status where needed, without narrative content
Correction ownership and reconciliation rules
in_practice.logs_to: The restricted exception register records rule failures, source-owner actions, resolution dates and released statistical versions without copying medical details.

evidence.claim: Deterministic validation can detect missing fields and inconsistent record sequences; the 75% saving depends on exception volumes and includes remaining follow-up.
Health data has special protection under GDPR Article 9.
The digest documents a Dutch fine partly associated with recording sickness causes, supporting exclusion of medical causes from this workflow.

risks: A valid open absence record could be incorrectly labelled an error.
Aggregated absence outputs can still expose health information in small groups.
Automated detection creates little benefit if source owners cannot resolve exceptions.
This statistical workflow does not replace Wet verbetering poortwachter case management or occupational-health responsibilities.
research_questions: Which validation rules identify confirmed errors with few false alarms?
How much total handling time remains across the analyst, HR Administration and Payroll?
Can AFAS provide the minimum necessary absence fields without medical causes or free text?
Who owns unresolved records, release tolerances and any separate statutory reporting approval?

tasks.short: Track regional labour-market and logistics trends that affect hiring and workforce plans.

today.trigger: A workforce-planning cycle, hard-to-fill vacancy or external development prompts a market scan.
steps: Search public labour-market statistics, logistics publications and relevant CAO updates.
Check publication dates, geographic coverage and the basis of each claim.
Compare external signals with Noordhaven's vacancies, offer acceptance and retention.
Discuss local conditions and uncertainty with Recruiters and HR Business Partners.
Prepare a sourced brief with possible implications and actions.
drudgery: Opening and summarising many similar articles
today.time_sinks: Checking whether a headline applies to Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo and separating evidence from vendor claims.

lenses.faster: A fixed source collection and one model step produce deduplicated summaries with citations and caveats. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 24 minutes for opening key sources, testing relevance and reviewing implications.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled scan collects approved sources and drafts a brief; the analyst approves every circulated interpretation. External conversations and changes to workforce plans stay with people.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: Recruiters review site-specific channel and offer-positioning choices weekly using current regional evidence. Demand would likely grow if a useful local brief becomes cheap to prepare.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reading repeated versions of the same press release. More time goes into local conversations and testing whether a trend actually changes Noordhaven's hiring choices.
lenses.options: Compare recruiting-channel changes, shift-pattern proposals and pay-review scenarios with explicit assumptions. The alternatives may change whether Noordhaven spends on sourcing, working conditions or compensation.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from collecting headlines to advising on workforce scenarios. Proposed authority to qualify evidence and recommend planning assumptions makes the role more expert, while pay and workforce decisions remain with their accountable owners.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's preparation of regional labour-market briefs; learn recruitment-channel economics and candidate feedback.
Absorb the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's initial collection of published market and CAO developments; learn benchmark comparability and collective-bargaining interpretation.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges local relevance, challenges causal claims and combines public evidence with trusted recruiter and manager conversations that a summary cannot replace.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one bounded summarisation step converts collected documents into a sourced draft using a fixed template. Open-ended agent exploration is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: The weekly regional workforce scan becomes due.
steps: Collect new material from an approved source list and retain publication dates and original links.
Remove duplicates and record geography, population and evidence type.
Run one model step to draft a source-linked brief distinguishing observations, claims and possible implications.
Have the analyst open material sources and compare signals with Noordhaven's hiring measures.
Approve the brief and route any proposed action to the responsible Recruiter, HR Business Partner or Compensation and Benefits Specialist.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every brief before circulation; accountable HR leaders approve workforce, compensation or shift changes and follow applicable CAO and OR processes.
data_needed: Original source text, dates, links and geographic scope
Relevant CAO publications and effective dates
Aggregated vacancy, time-to-hire and offer-acceptance measures
Site-level mature starter-cohort retention
Recruiter and HR Business Partner feedback with personal details removed
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint evidence library stores collected sources, the draft, analyst corrections, approval and any later decision or outcome.

evidence.claim: The digest's Workday workforce-report example does not establish how much of the reported change AI caused, illustrating the need to preserve causal caveats.
Bounded source summarisation can reduce reading and drafting effort; the 60% saving is a planning estimate and does not apply to external relationship work.

risks: National or international findings may not apply to a specific Dutch logistics labour market.
Multiple articles can repeat one weak source and appear to provide independent confirmation.
A model may omit a qualification, invent a citation or confuse proposed and effective CAO changes.
A trend correlation can be mistaken for evidence that a particular intervention will improve 90-day retention.
research_questions: Are sufficiently current and comparable sources available for all three regional labour markets?
Does the draft preserve dates, geographic limits and causal caveats accurately?
Do weekly briefs change a named recruitment or workforce decision enough to justify their preparation?
How much of today's task is source processing versus local conversations that remain human?

role.altitude: The role becomes the steward of Noordhaven's workforce measurement and HR information service: less report assembly, more reliable definitions, source quality, access, scenario evaluation and manager support. Proposed decision rights include approving technical releases, withholding unreliable figures and prioritising the analytics backlog; HR, Payroll and Finance retain their substantive employment and financial authorities.
reach: HR Business Partner: recurring workforce packs and preparation of information-needs reviews; develop site operations knowledge and stakeholder interviewing.
HR Administrator: routine data-quality detection and correction-queue preparation; develop AFAS workflow knowledge while leaving source corrections with authorised owners.
Recruiter: sourced regional labour-market briefs; develop recruitment economics and candidate-market knowledge.
Learning and Development Specialist: certificate-status reporting and dashboard guidance; develop certificate-validity and shift-worker learning knowledge.
Payroll Specialist and Controller: preparation of workforce-count and payroll-reporting reconciliations; develop CAO pay-component, period and ledger knowledge.
FP&A Analyst: workforce-volume inputs and scenario-tool construction; develop financial modelling and explicit assumption management.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover 894.5 supplied annual hours, about 56% of the role. Savings are planning estimates for established workflows after implementation, not measured results or a headcount reduction; integration work, source-owner follow-up, changing definitions and service demand limit released capacity.
skills_to_grow: Power BI semantic modelling, DAX, SQL and reproducible reconciliation
